Fixes #110018

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

The kubelet's `--cloud-provider` flag is deprecated but still has a legitimate use case.  The in-tree values "aws, ..." should be are deprecated.  The empty string and "external" values need to be distinct, because "external" instructs kubelet to taint nodes for the external cloud provider. 

There is already a deprecation notice when the in-tree values are selected at: https://github.com/kubernetes/cloud-provider/blob/master/plugins.go#L132.  An alternative (and the original proposal) is to rely on that deprecation notice which targets the deprecated values, and undeprecate the `--cloud-provider` flag.

```release-note
A boolean alternative to kubelet's deprecated `--cloud-provider` flag was added (`ExternalCloudProvider`), because only the in-tree values are deprecated.  The need to specify whether or not an external cloud provider is running is still necessary.
```

Rather than undeprecating this do we want to consider adding an `ExternalCloudProvider` KubeletConfiguration option? - I don't think we want to support more than `none` or `external` long term, so keeping a free text flag seems like an unnecessarily complex api.

That's definitely an option.  The tradeoff is the effort required by deployments to change their configuration to the new flag.   I'm not sure I think the API improvement is enough to justify making everyone change their kubelet flags, but I agree it is slightly better.

Adding my (unsolicited) 2¢...

If there is only going to be a single configuration allowed for `--cloud-provider` going forward (expressed with one or the other sentinel strings `""` or `"external"`) then it would be functionally equivalent to simply deprecate the flag. Once the deprecation milestone is reached, the kubelet is only going to be able to do one thing in this configuration surface area, so why would we want to require the user to explicitly declare the required configuration string in the kubelet args? Seems like a secret handshake UX, not sure that's improving things.
@jackfrancis Not sure I understand your point of view. There is a need for a `--cloud-provider` like flag in the future.

@hakman of course, if `--cloud-provider` can express multiple configuration options then it makes sense to retain it. I was simply responding to an earlier comment that suggests that `--cloud-provider` is going to be locked down to `""|"external"` (both strings indicating an equivalent configuration). If I'm wrong about that then my comment can be ignored.

@jackfrancis Maybe there is a misunderstanding:
* `""` - for clusters that are not cloud aware, no taint will be added (like those created with `kubeadm`).
* `external` - for clusters that are cloud aware, adds `node.cloudprovider.kubernetes.io/uninitialized:NoSchedule` taint.

Sure, one could still debate which one should be the default in the future and if `""` is a good value, in general. At least this is my also unsolicited view on things. 😄

@hakman thanks for the clarification. Given that those configuration values have meaning over time, it's probably easiest to just keep them.

Next time I'll just read the code. :)

@endocrimes I think we should move forward one way or the other.  I can make the `ExternalCloudProvider` change in addition, but I think we need to undeprecate or at least remove the reference to `1.24`.

If we add the value to KubeletConfiguration, then the logic would be that if either `KubeletConfiguration.ExternalCloudProvider` is `true` or `--cloud-provider` is `external` then we consider the cloud provider to be external and we taint nodes.  Ideally we could ignore `--cloud-provider` if we find that `KubeletConfiguration.ExternalCloudProvider` was set, but I've tried to do that and I didn't find a good way.  So assuming we are ok with having two different places for the same piece of configuration with the those semantics, while the flag is being deprecated, then I'll go ahead and make the change to the PR.
/retest
@endocrimes this is ready for another look if you have a second, I've given your suggestion an attempt.

issue_context.title: kubelet without deprecated `--cloud-provider=external` do not get proper taint and are not CCM initialized
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

The [kubelet CLI docs](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/command-line-tools-reference/kubelet/) state that `--cloud-provider=external` is deprecated and will go away in1.24:

> 
> --cloud-provider string
> --
>  | The provider for cloud services. Set to empty string for running with no cloud provider. If set, the cloud provider > determines the name of the node (consult cloud provider documentation to determine if and how the hostname is used). (DEPRECATED: will be removed in 1.24 or later, in favor of removing cloud provider code from Kubelet.)

The [docs for running a CCM](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/running-cloud-controller/#running-cloud-controller-manager), on the other hand, say that `--cloud-provider=external` is required, in order to get the proper `node.cloudprovider.kubernetes.io/uninitialized` taint.

I launched a single-node 1.23 cluster without `--cloud-provider=external`, and while I did not get the deprecation warnings, the node was not properly tainted, and the CCM I am running never seems to get the correct calls leading to populating the providerID and removing the taint.

I do not know if this is a bug in the controller-manager and/or kubelet, or that we need to do something else to get this to work, and thus missing documentation. 



### What did you expect to happen?

node to get the correct taint, k8s to initialize the node.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Launch a single node cluster without `--cloud-provider=external`
2. See that the node does not have the taint
3. Launch a CCM
4. See that it does not set the provider ID

### Anything else we need to know?

/triage accepted

I don't think the `node.cloudprovider.kubernetes.io/uninitialized` taint can be added to clusters without the flag passed, because that could break legitimate clusters where the flag isn't passed and a CCM isn't run.  I think the messaging is definitely confusing and we need to improve the documentation.  The `--cloud-provider=external` should probably not be deprecated, rather, the flag should specify that passing the values `aws`, .. etc are deprecated.
@nckturner Would it be a good idea to have also `--cloud-provider=none` which would make clear the taint wouldn't be applied? I guess it would also be the default.

Agreed on cases where you don't need a CCM, that it should not taint them. 

It sounds like it should not be deprecated at all, but rather should have two acceptable values:

- "none" - do not taint, no CCM expected (default)
- "external" - taint, expect CCM 


Is that it?
:+1:  It seems reasonable to have an explicit value for the case with no ccm and no taint, and to make that default.
Beyond the future plans, what is the right thing to do for 1.23 and 1.24?
Well, assuming you are running a CCM and are expecting a taint, you should use `--cloud-provider=external`.
Even though it is marked as deprecated in 1.23 and supposed to be removed in 1.24?

> Even though it is marked as deprecated in 1.23 and supposed to be removed in 1.24?

Probably this should be addressed and cherry-picked in 1.23 and 1.24.

> Probably this should be addressed and cherry-picked in 1.23 and 1.24.

+1.  Let me take a stab at this now.
I didn't change the empty value to "none" yet in the above PR, but its still on the table.  Figured I'd go with minimal change for the first iteration and see what people think.
